question: Should `recomby-ai/promptly-prompt` be admitted to the ClawHub catalog as a plugin package, redirected to skill-only self-publishing, or declined after hook/security review?
rationale: The repository has package publishing surfaces, but accepting a third-party prompt-submission hook requires maintainer choice on catalog family, prompt trust boundary, provenance, license terms, and namespace ownership.

options.title: Review for plugin admission
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers verify package shape, OpenClaw manifest/compatibility metadata, source provenance, and hook security before publication.

options.title: Redirect to self-published skill
options.body: Close or narrow the plugin intake if maintainers decide this should only be published by the author as a ClawHub skill rather than an OpenClaw plugin package.

options.title: Decline catalog listing
options.body: Decline publication if the prompt-intercepting hook behavior or package provenance does not meet ClawHub trust and transparency expectations.

recommendation.title: Review for plugin admission
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers verify package shape, OpenClaw manifest/compatibility metadata, source provenance, and hook security before publication.

likelyOwner.reason: The current plugin catalog and package-validation surfaces route through Patrick-Erichsen's recent main-branch history, making him the best available owner for the catalog-path decision.
